kinds.name: io
kinds.role: I/O tile: two PIO pads and their routing

kinds.name: logic
kinds.role: PLB: eight logic cells (LUT4, flip-flop, carry) and their routing

kinds.name: ramb
kinds.role: EBR, bottom half (each EBR spans a ramb and the ramt above it)

bitstream.command_form: one byte, high nibble the command, low nibble the argument's length in bytes, then the argument big-endian

command_meanings.6: next data's width in bits, less one
command_meanings.0 1: CRAM data follows, then two zero bytes
command_meanings.0 3: block RAM data follows, then two zero bytes
command_meanings.2: CRC-16 of the bytes since the CRC reset
command_meanings.9: option bits; bit mask 1 is icepack -s (no deep sleep)

crc.covers: bytes after the reset command, up to and including the CRC command's byte

options.no_bram: icepack -n leaves out the block RAM data commands

bitstream.tile_bit: B{r}[{c}] of a tile is CRAM bank `bank`, line line0 + layout.rows[r], position pos0 + layout.cols[c]
bitstream.ram_bit: word w, bit k of a block RAM is block RAM bank `bank`, line w, position pos0 + ram_bits[k]; .ram_data X Y names it by its ramb tile
bitstream.extra_bit: .extra_bit BANK POS LINE is CRAM bank BANK, line LINE, position POS

logic_cell.lut_index: index i = in_0 + 2 in_1 + 4 in_2 + 8 in_3: the LUT's output when the inputs are those bits

flip_flop.verilog: always @(posedge clk) if (cen) x <= sr ? 1'b0 : lout;
always @(posedge clk) if (cen) x <= sr ? 1'b1 : lout;
always @(posedge clk, posedge sr) if (sr) x <= 1'b0; else if (cen) x <= lout;
always @(posedge clk, posedge sr) if (sr) x <= 1'b1; else if (cen) x <= lout;
always @(negedge clk) if (cen) x <= sr ? 1'b0 : lout;
always @(negedge clk) if (cen) x <= sr ? 1'b1 : lout;
always @(negedge clk, posedge sr) if (sr) x <= 1'b0; else if (cen) x <= lout;
always @(negedge clk, posedge sr) if (sr) x <= 1'b1; else if (cen) x <= lout;

carry.with CarryInSet: assign co = (in_1 & in_2) | ((in_1 | in_2) & ci); assign ci = 1;

logic_cell.names: in_0..in_3 the cell's inputs, lout the LUT's output, out the cell's output, co carry out, ci the tile's carry_in_mux (the first cell's carry in), clk/cen/sr the tile's shared clock, enable and set/reset, x a net with none of these names

block_ram.source: icebox (functions: chipdb's RamConfig and RamCascade; parameters: Lattice's SB_RAM40_4K, whose READ_MODE and WRITE_MODE 0 to 3 are 256x16, 512x8, 1024x4 and 2048x2)
block_ram.functions: the SB_RAM40_4K parameters icebox_vlog gives with each function alone set (on a base where that is needed), or omitted if it shows no RAM
block_ram.ports: each port bit: the RAM's tile (0 the ramb, 1 the ramt above it) and the net there

io_cell.type: six characters, PINTYPE_0 first: 1 where the bit is set
io_cell.names: pad the pin; d_in_0, d_in_1, d_out_0, d_out_1, out_enb the cell's ports; clk_en, in_clk, out_clk, latch the I/O tile's shared ones; r0, r1... its registers; x a net with none of these names. Where the verilog says nothing about the pad, icebox_vlog drives nothing

tile_functions.note: non-routing settings of each kind of tile, by IceStorm's names; LC_k is a logic cell's 20 bits (see logic_cell)

pins.note: package pin: the I/O tile and its PIO (z)

gbufin.note: I/O tile (x, y) whose fabout drives global network g

gbufpin.note: the pad (x, y, z) that can drive global network g

colbuf.note: column buffer at (x, y) feeds tile (x, y)

ieren.note: PIO (x, y, z) has its IE/REN bits in PIO (x, y, z)

cells.note: special-purpose cells; each port or setting is a name in a tile (a net or a configuration bit)

attrs.LOCKED: cb81 cm36 cm49 qn48 swg16tr vq100

routing.note: a switch drives dst from one source, chosen by its bits' values (first bit first); names are the tile's own names for nets. Every tile with switches has one switch box. A net shape lists its tiles and names relative to its lowest (x, then y) tile, and is placed with that tile at every position of each rectangle [x0, x1, y0, y1]

board.method: designs made from this description and packed by Epitome, programmed with icesprog, A3 (from the iCELink's UART) passed to B3 (to its UART) through the logic under test; the Mac sends 64 bytes at 115200 baud and sees them come back (echo), nothing (silent) or something else (other:N)

findings.finding: every logic cell's LUT is where the description says: each cell passes A3 to B3
each LUT input's bits are where the description says: a table following input j passes it, the inverse table does not
an unrouted LUT input reads 0: a table true only at index 2^j passes input j
IoCtrl.IE set turns a pin's input off (A3 then reads nothing); IoCtrl.REN does not stop a driven input
the global network reaches a tile only through its column buffer (ColBufCtrl in the colbuf tile)
the flip-flop clocks from D1 (the iCELink's 12 MHz) on either edge, with NegClk
an unrouted flip-flop enable reads 1 and an unrouted set/reset 0, synchronous or not, set or reset
a block RAM reads its .ram_data contents: word 1 at RADDR[0] = A3, clocked from D1, RE driven to 1
each RDATA bit is the word's bit of the same number, as .ram_data and the port map say
RamConfig.PowerUp set turns the LP1K's block RAM off, and an unrouted RE reads 0 (as icebox_vlog says)
the write port writes: WDATA[0] = A3 into word 0 each clock, read back; MASK[0] set stops the bit being written, and unrouted it reads 0
in 512x8, 1024x4 and 2048x2 a data pin reads the bit board::ram_mode_bit gives, and no other
in the same write modes, a data pin writes the bit board::ram_mode_bit gives, and not its neighbour
the carry is (in_1 & in_2) | ((in_1 | in_2) & ci): with CarryInSet ci is 1 and the carry follows in_1; without it the first cell's ci is 0

ram_modes.note: the stored bit (word*16 + bit) a data pin reads at an address in read modes 1 to 3 (512x8, 1024x4, 2048x2), each found on the board by binary search: B3 = A3 AND RDATA[pin] echoes when the RAM gives 1. The word is the address's low eight bits; the data pins are those with pin % 2^m = 2^(m-1) - 1, each reading bit (pin with its low m bits clear) + (address >> 8) (board::ram_mode_bit); predicted is that formula's bit
